Women and teenagers dying from pregnancy and childbirth complications

Women and girls living with untreated obstetric fistula

overview: Madagascar's women's health landscape is driven overwhelmingly by government, UN, and NGO maternal and reproductive health programs rather than a commercial femtech startup scene. The country has one of the world's highest maternal mortality ratios and heavy unmet need for family planning, addressed largely through a network of over 20,000 community health volunteers, UNFPA-supported midwifery and contraceptive supply, and mHealth tools like CommCare. A small local digital health sector exists (e.g. MEDDoC), but 2025 US foreign aid cuts sharply disrupted contraceptive supply and mobile clinics, making donor dependence the defining feature of the ecosystem.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent developments are dominated by the fallout of 2025 aid cuts and continued maternal health campaigns.

items.text: US foreign aid freeze ends UNFPA support for MSI Madagascar, which had received 100% of its family planning commodities (implants, IUDs, injectables) plus outreach funding from UNFPA.
USAID clawed back approved funding across seven countries including Madagascar; Madagascar received a rescission of termination notice allowing some projects to continue.
Free obstetric fistula screening and repair campaign runs at the Regional Referral Hospital in Antsohihy (18-22 August), delivered by Freedom From Fistula Madagascar.

Report on training midwives to bridge Madagascar's maternal health gap: students lack computers and connectivity, and funding cuts mean graduates must now find jobs themselves rather than being recruited directly into public service.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National strategies frame community health, family planning, and digital health, with ambitious 2030 targets.

items.text: Strategie Nationale de Sante Digitale de Madagascar 2023-2027 sets the framework for digital health, including mHealth for community agents.
Plan Strategique National de la Sante Communautaire 2023-2027 structures the community health worker system that delivers maternal, neonatal, and family planning services.
Plan d'Action National Budgetise en Planification Familiale targets raising modern contraceptive prevalence to 60% and cutting unmet need to 8% by 2030.
UNFPA global Start with Her strategy for reproductive, maternal and newborn health 2025-2030 frames its country-level support including Madagascar.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Activity centers on incubated digital health startups, community mHealth tools, and menstrual health social enterprise.

items.text: MEDDoC, a Malagasy startup digitizing the health system with online appointment booking and telemedicine (including a planned platform for rural populations), incubated by Zafy Tody and selected for Miary Digital.
USAID Mikolo / Ministry of Health developed a CommCare mHealth app enabling community health agents to manage childhood illness, give family planning advice, and refer severe cases.
SEED Madagascar, with UNICEF, runs a menstrual hygiene management program in the Anosy region, training seamstresses to make and sell reusable sanitary pads as a livelihood.
Sante Sud installs self-employed community midwives in rural fokontany delivery clinics in the Analamanga region to extend care to women and children.
Miary Digital second cohort (launched Jan 2025) drew 320 applications; 26 startups selected, each eligible for USD 15,000 on completing incubation.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: There is little venture funding; capital flows are donor grants and public innovation subsidies rather than equity rounds.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The ecosystem is anchored by government programs, UN agencies, NGOs, and a few local digital health ventures and incubators.

sections.heading: Active investors
sections.narrative: Funding is dominated by development donors and public innovation programs; private gender-lens venture capital is largely absent locally.

items.name: UNFPA
items.role: Primary financier of reproductive health commodities, midwifery, and family planning in Madagascar

items.name: USAID
items.role: Funded Mikolo/ACCESS mHealth and community health programs; 2025 cuts disrupted family planning supply

items.name: UNICEF
items.role: Backs menstrual hygiene management and community health volunteer programs

items.role: Funds the Miary Digital startup incubation program that supports digital health ventures
